title: token-rotation-mechanism
intention: A token posted on the cairn device's announce feed rotates through every device in alpha order — each device's probe fires, runs its sleep cycle or forwards, and the rotation completes back to start.
why: One token rotation replaces N independent sleep daemons — the same move the ground loop made for heartbeats. Serial by design because of measured OOM history (n=3) and because we don't yet know which sleep cycles are independent. The probe pattern is the mechanism: a three-line custom probe (match, decide, forward) is a valid implementation; no shim overhead, no bus routing, no LLM needed (Akien, 2026-08-24).
traces_to: Telos aim 5 (self-improving) — the rotation gives each device its maintenance window
Law 4 — the token on the bus is physics: a device's probe fires because a message arrived, not a schedule
Shrinking-footprint derivation — one token rotation vs N independent daemons

proves_green.proof_gate: tester — a token posted on the announce feed rotates through at least one device and returns, proved by teeth a hollow build could not pass

falsifier.proves_red: DONE when a token can be posted, received by at least one device, forwarded through the roster, and return to the cairn device with at least one real sleep cycle executed. WRONG INTENT if the rotation mechanism is the wrong shape — e.g., devices need to sleep concurrently, or the bus is the wrong transport.
falsifier.horizon: first complete rotation is the first measurement

how: The cairn device posts a sleep-cycle token on its announce feed. Each device has a three-line probe that matches the token, checks whether it is that device's turn in alpha order (from the ground loop's roster), runs its sleep cycle if it is, and forwards the token to the next device. The last device forwards back to the cairn device, completing the rotation.

AS SETTLED IN PASS 5 (folded so this step reads whole) — MEASURED HOLDINGS, 2026-09-18, so no step below need assume a cited primitive exists (the reader has no repository; this paragraph IS the repository for these names): (h1) cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/discovery.py:71 `device_folders(root: Path | None = None, folder_name: str = "probes") -> list[tuple[str, Path]]` — every (device_id, probes_folder) on disk under root (the repo when None), sorted; device_id is the probes folder's parent name; :100 `load_module(path: Path)` imports a .py by path and returns the module. (h4) cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/bus.py:202 `BusDevice.scratch(prefix="bus_traffic", device_id="bus")` (classmethod) — a throwaway Postgres-backed bus with `.close()`; :361 `post(*, sender, to, channel, why, verb="", body=None, reply_to=None) -> dict` (the envelope, with an `id`); :420 `read(*, to=None, channel=None, ...) -> list[dict]`; :444 `request(...)`. Delivery happens ONLY on channel "personal" and only once a shim's first pulse has wired it (`wire_delivery`); "announce" is a record channel read back with `bus.read(to=..., channel="announce")`. (h5) cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/loop.py:77 `GroundLoopDevice(device_id="ground_loop", liveness_home=None, ..., bus=None)`; :106 `.subscribe(shim)`; :237 `.beat(now, context: dict | None = None) -> dict` pulses every subscribed shim in subscription order with the SAME context dict. (h6) cairn/tools/base/shim.py `BaseShim(bus=...)`: `_presence` (:249, NEVER_BOOTED | ONLINE | OFFLINE from cairn.tools.base.shim); :296 `probes(self) -> list[Probe]` (override to hand back loaded probes); `_start_device(self)` (:56/:513, the wake hook — returns the device object); :380 `on_pulse(now, context)` runs each probe's trigger and, when true, `_fire` (:533) posts `bus.post(sender=self.device_id, to=cb.to, verb=cb.verb, channel=cb.channel, why=cb.why, body=cb.payload(context))`; :750 `deliver(envelope)`: a VERBED envelope is looked up in `device.declared_verbs()` (unknown verb -> bounce; a dict result is posted back to envelope["sender"] on personal with why "<verb> reply"), a VERB-LESS envelope goes to `device.receive(envelope)`. (h7) cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/discovered.py:116 `_FeedbackDevice.receive(envelope) -> dict` writes {finding: envelope why, inspector_target: device_id, probe_source: sender, envelope_id: envelope id, verb, body} to its inbound DataRecorder and returns {accepted: True, device}; it declares NO verbs. So a verb-less personal envelope to a discovered device LANDS in its inbox and a verbed one BOUNCES — measured, not assumed. (h8) cairn/tools/base/probe.py:303 `Probe` is a frozen dataclass with fields why, trigger(now, context) -> bool, to, verb="", channel="personal", body={}, carry(context) -> dict | None, while_true=False, enough=None, horizon=None; `payload(context)` is body with carry's fragment merged over; :442 `once(context, key, compute)` as D5 states. (h9) cairn/machines/build_inspector (proof_coverage): `declared(proof_path)` reads the module-level PROVES with ast.literal_eval; `clauses(ticket)` lists the falsifier's clause names — an unnumbered falsifier is the single clause "all". (h10) an existing proof in exactly D7's shape to read beside it: cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_delivery_poke.py (BusDevice.scratch, hand-held shims, beats, PROVES, _run_all). BUILD ORDER across the decisions: D1 (folders + charter), then D3 (roster) and D4 (the standing cycle) — both leaves — then D2 (mint / hand / receive_answer / close, which CALL roster and the cycle store by the contracts D3 and D4 state), then D5 (the device-side helper), then D6 (nothing to build), then D7 (the proof). A decision's number is its address, not its build order. The `what` of the charter names FIVE callables of token.py — roster, mint, receive_answer, standing, and cycle_dir — plus the private _hand/_announce/_close it composes; 'five' counts the public names.

SHAPE: HUB, NOT RELAY — measured. `Probe.to` is a static field (cairn/tools/base/probe.py, the Probe dataclass; shim.py:545 posts to `cb.to` verbatim) and a probe may not import the cairn device's roster (no cross-device imports), so a device's three-line probe CANNOT address 'the next device'. Therefore the cairn device HANDS the token to each device in turn and every device answers back to cairn, which hands to the next: (a) `token.mint(bus, *, roots=None, roster_root=None, now=None)` opens a cycle {cycle_id: uuid hex, roster: D3, position: 0, visited: [], opened_at, closed_at: None, closed_by: None}, writes it (D4) and hands to roster[0]; (b) a HAND is `bus.post(sender="cairn", to=<device>, channel="personal", verb="", why="sleep token", body={"sleep_token": cycle_id, "position": i, "of": n})` — verb-less BECAUSE a verbed envelope to a discovered device bounces (shim.deliver: `_FeedbackDevice` declares no verbs) while a verb-less one lands in its inbound DataRecorder via receive(); (c) the device's probe answers by poking `to="cairn", verb="sleep-token", channel="personal"`, body={"sleep_token": cycle_id, "device": <id>, "answer": <what its sleep work returned>}; (d) CairnDevice.declared_verbs() grows `sleep-token` → `_handle_sleep_token(envelope)` = `token.receive_answer(bus, envelope["body"], roots=..., now=...)`: an answer whose sleep_token != the standing open cycle_id, or from a device that is not roster[position], is REFUSED loudly — emit `sleep_token_refused`, return {"accepted": False, "reason": ...}, cycle untouched; an accepted answer appends {device, answer, at} to visited, advances position, and either hands to the next device or CLOSES the cycle (closed_at, closed_by="rotation complete"); returns {"accepted": True, "cycle_id": ..., "position": ..., "closed": bool}. HANDLER RESULTS NEVER CARRY THE KEY `sleep_token` (the shim posts the result back to the device as a reply, which lands in the same inbound recorder the probe reads — D5 matches on that key). (e) a second verb `sleep-cycle` → `_handle_sleep_cycle(envelope)` with body {"act": "mint"} (= mint) or {"act": "show"} (= the standing cycle.json, or {"cycle": None}). (f) THE ANNOUNCE FEED IS THE RECORD OF THE ROTATION: every hand and the close each post ONE record `bus.post(sender="cairn", to="cairn", channel="announce", why="sleep token", verb="", body={"cycle_id", "event": "hand"|"closed", "device", "position", "of"})` — announce has no delivery (bus.py: delivery only on personal), so it is a record, never a transport; a complete rotation over n devices leaves exactly n+1 announce records for that cycle_id. AS SETTLED IN PASS 1 (folded so this step reads whole) — In receive_answer(), after appending the visit and incrementing position, the cycle CLOSES when position == len(roster) (closed_by "rotation complete", one announce record with event "closed"); otherwise it HANDS to roster[position] (one announce record with event "hand"). So n devices leave exactly n+1 announce records for the cycle_id. AS SETTLED IN PASS 5 (folded so this step reads whole) — roster() is D3's function and the cycle store is D4's; D2 builds AFTER both and calls them by the contracts stated there (see the BUILD ORDER in D1). The hand is verb-less on personal BECAUSE of holding (h7) in D1: a discovered device declares no verbs, so a verbed hand would bounce while a verb-less one lands in its inbound DataRecorder through receive(); routing is by the RECIPIENT'S declared verbs, and an empty verb means 'receive'. AS SETTLED IN PASS 7 (folded so this step reads whole) — THE VERB TABLE, spelled out: BaseDevice.declared_verbs() (cairn/tools/base/device.py) returns a dict {verb_name: bound handler}; a handler takes the envelope dict and returns a dict (the shim posts that dict back to the sender as the reply). CairnDevice extends it exactly so: `def declared_verbs(self) -> dict: return {**super().declared_verbs(), "sleep-token": self._handle_sleep_token, "sleep-cycle": self._handle_sleep_cycle}`; `def _handle_sleep_token(self, envelope): from cairn.devices.cairn.machines.sleep_cycle import token; result = token.receive_answer(self._bus, envelope.get("body") or {}, roots=self._roots); if not result.get("accepted"): self.emit("sleep_token_refused", pointer=str(result.get("device")), values=dict(result)); return result`; `def _handle_sleep_cycle(self, envelope): ... act = (envelope.get("body") or {}).get("act"); if act == "mint": return {"cycle": token.mint(self._bus, roots=self._roots, roster_root=self._roster_root)}; if act == "show": return {"cycle": token.standing(self._roots)}; return {"accepted": False, "reason": "sleep-cycle takes act mint|show"}`. The imports of token are INSIDE the handlers (a hollow build that lacks token.py reds at call time, not at import). CairnDevice.__init__(self, bus=None, roots=None, roster_root=None) stores self._bus, self._roots, self._roster_root (D4/D7's seam).

ROSTER. `token.roster(root=None) -> list[str]`: alpha-sorted, de-duplicated device ids from `cairn.devices.cairn.machines.ground_loop.discovery.device_folders(root)` (the ground loop's own roster, read from disk every time — never cached), FILTERED to folders that hold the file `token.SLEEP_PROBE == "sleeps_when_the_token_arrives.py"`. Opt-in by file, measured 2026-09-18: device_folders() returned 43 probes folders and 0 of them carry a sleep probe, so an unfiltered token would be handed to a device with nothing to answer it and the rotation would stall at position 0 forever. A device joins the rotation by berthing that one file in its probes/ folder (D5 makes it three lines) and leaves it by deleting the file — the same physics as the ground loop's roster. An EMPTY roster closes the cycle at mint with closed_by="nothing to visit" and one announce record (event "closed", of=0). AS SETTLED IN PASS 4 (folded so this step reads whole) — token.py DEFINES the module constant `SLEEP_PROBE = "sleeps_when_the_token_arrives.py"` at module top, above roster(), beside `TOKEN_KEY = "sleep_token"` (the body key every hand carries and every answer echoes) and `DEVICE = "cairn"`; roster() reads `(Path(folder) / SLEEP_PROBE).is_file()` for each (device_id, folder) that device_folders(root) yields. AS SETTLED IN PASS 5 (folded so this step reads whole) — device_folders is holding (h1) in D1: `list[tuple[str, Path]]` of (device_id, probes folder), and `(Path(folder) / SLEEP_PROBE).is_file()` is a plain pathlib test on that folder.

STATE. The standing cycle lives in instance-space at `instance_path("cairn", 0, roots) / "machines" / "sleep_cycle" / "cycle.json"` (cairn.tools.base.address.instance_path; roots=None is the live ~/.cairn) — the whole dict of D2(a), rewritten atomically (write to cycle.json.tmp then os.replace) on every change. `token.standing(roots=None) -> dict | None` reads it. mint() while a cycle is OPEN supersedes it: the open cycle is appended as one line to `superseded.jsonl` beside cycle.json with superseded_at, then the new cycle replaces it (Law 7: the old record is kept, corrected by a later line). Closed cycles stay in cycle.json until the next mint. No runtime state in the repo. AS SETTLED IN PASS 5 (folded so this step reads whole) — instance_path is holding (h2) in D1 with exactly the three-parameter signature `instance_path(device, instance=0, roots=None)`; atomic replacement is `tmp.write_text(...)` then `os.replace(tmp, cycle.json)` — POSIX rename, atomic on one filesystem.

DEVICE-SIDE HELPER: cairn/tools/base/mail_probe.py, `answers_mail(key, handle, *, device_file, why, to="cairn", verb="", horizon=1000) -> Probe`. device_id = Path(device_file).resolve().parent.parent.name (the probes/ folder's parent — the same rule discovery.device_folders uses). Inbound = DataRecorder(instance_path(device_id, 0, roots) / "tools" / "data_recorder" / "inbound") — exactly where `_FeedbackDevice.receive` (ground_loop/discovered.py) lands a discovered device's mail — with roots = context.get("roots") (None live; a proof hands fixture roots in the beat context). Answered = DataRecorder(... / "tools" / "data_recorder" / "answered"). PENDING = inbound records whose body is a dict carrying `key` and whose envelope_id is not in the answered recorder's envelope_ids, in write order. trigger(now, context) is true iff pending is non-empty; the survey is memoised with probe.once(context, f"mail_probe:{device_id}:{key}", ...) — keyed by device because the beat's context is SHARED across every shim. carry(context) takes the OLDEST pending record, calls `handle(body) -> answer` (the device's sleep work, whatever it is), writes an answered record {finding: f"answered {key}", inspector_target: device_id, probe_source: "mail_probe", envelope_id, answer} and returns the poke body {key: body[key], "device": device_id, "answer": answer}. enough never (a mailbox never retires). while_true=True so two tokens in one beat are answered on consecutive beats instead of the second waiting for the trigger to fall. A device's sleep probe is then three lines: `from cairn.tools.base.mail_probe import answers_mail` / `def _sleep(body): return <its work>` / `PROBE = answers_mail("sleep_token", _sleep, device_file=__file__, why="...", verb="sleep-token")`. The base charter cairn/tools/base/intention+why.json gets ONE added invoke line naming mail_probe (its `what` enumerates the modules) and recompile_gate.sh runs in the same act. AS SETTLED IN PASS 3 (folded so this step reads whole) — probe.once EXISTS, nothing is extended: `once(context: dict | None, key: str, compute: Callable[[], object])` at cairn/tools/base/probe.py:442. `context` is the beat's one dict (ground_loop.beat hands the SAME dict to every shim's on_pulse, and on_pulse hands it to fires / payload / gathered_enough of one probe); `key` names the slot; `compute` is a ZERO-ARG callable run at most once per beat. The memo berths under context['_once'] keyed by (compute.__module__, compute.__qualname__, key); an injected context[key] wins over the memo; a raise is not memoised. No timeout, no third-argument variants. `roots` is in the context only when the caller puts it there — live the ground loop passes none, so context.get('roots') is None and instance_path resolves to ~/.cairn; a proof passes {'roots': <fixture roots>} into loop.beat(now, context). The base charter's field is `invoke`, a single STRING of backtick-quoted import lines separated by '; ' (not a list); the added line is `from cairn.tools.base.mail_probe import answers_mail` appended in that same shape; the charter's `what` field is prose and is unchanged (the parenthetical's `what` meant 'the field that enumerates the modules', which is `invoke`). AS SETTLED IN PASS 4 (folded so this step reads whole) — `while_true` is an EXISTING field of cairn.tools.base.probe.Probe (probe.py:360, default False): with it True the shim pokes on EVERY pulse the trigger holds true instead of once per rising edge. answers_mail does NOT loop: each beat, carry() answers exactly ONE record — the oldest pending — and returns one poke body; a second pending token is answered on the NEXT beat because the trigger is still true and while_true keeps the probe firing. answers_mail passes `while_true=True` straight into the Probe(...) constructor; it takes no such parameter of its own. AS SETTLED IN PASS 5 (folded so this step reads whole) — DataRecorder is holding (h3) in D1 (write(record) / read() -> list), BaseShim._fire and _FeedbackDevice.receive are (h6)/(h7), probe.once is (h8). mail_probe does NOT use SLEEP_PROBE: the constant lives in token.py (D3) and mail_probe is a base tool that knows nothing of the sleep cycle; the only name the two share is the body key string "sleep_token", which the device's three-liner passes as `key`. AS SETTLED IN PASS 6 (folded so this step reads whole) — MEASURED 2026-09-18: cairn/tools/base/intention+why.json EXISTS (a base-tool charter, component "base"); its `invoke` is one string that begins `import: ` and holds 10 backtick-quoted import lines separated by "; " (core_values, device, shim, probe, address, ...); the edit is to append "; `from cairn.tools.base.mail_probe import answers_mail`" to that string, nothing else in the charter changes. recompile_gate.sh EXISTS at cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/recompile_gate.sh (executable, 2298 bytes, owned by the intentions_model_compiler tool): it is the WRITE GATE of the compiled intentions model — a source (any beside-code intention+why.json, or an intentions-not-beside-code entry) changed, so the writer pokes it and it regenerates CairnCommons/intentions-congruency-lab/ (a copy of every charter, one file each); it is invoked by EVENTS only (the writer, in the same act as the charter write), never by a clock, and it always exits 0 so it cannot block its caller.
